decisions.statement: A page leaving which workload is meant unsettled is refused.
A cluster already standing as the page describes is applied nothing.
A web app is built from its source before the web app is put up.
The source built is the commit the deploy names.
The commit built is proved to install before anything is applied.
An install is proved against the manifests the commit tracks rather than against the worktree.
A commit whose tracked manifests do not install refuses the call.
A commit origin main does not carry is pushed there before anything is built.
Nothing is applied and nothing is built before origin main has the commit.
The push carries the branch this checkout is on rather than the commit alone.
A push that fails refuses the call and names the commit origin main still wants.
A push leaving the commit uncarried refuses the call rather than building on.
A build already made from that commit is made again by nothing.
A build is made before a manifest is applied.
The pod a build is reported in is the pod serving once every rollout is done.
What a pod serves and what a build made are reported under labels sharing no prefix.
The pod a build ran in is named by nothing the report carries.
A pod starts on a build kept beside the package that pod runs from.
A manifest moving that package rolls out a pod with no build to start on.
A value the build needs that nothing has is refused before anything is applied.
A value the build needs is reported by its name rather than by the text the value has.
A kubectl that refuses makes the call refuse.
A change standing only in the worktree is not built.
Nothing here puts up a service the cluster does not run as a workload.
A dry run pushes nothing and says what the push would carry.
The manifests and what the build needs are read from the tree pinned at the commit.

definition: the web app a deploy names, put up onto the cluster its page describes
